core.title: Decompose plans by user-facing jobs, not by how the system is built
core.given: A planner is decomposing source material into plan items (plan artifacts).
core.then: Each plan item states what the system does — a user-facing job it performs (domain capability) — not how it is built.
prefer: Reframe an implementation-flavored source item to the user-facing job it serves.
Alternatively, route an implementation decision (a technology choice) to tests or architecture decision records instead of the plan.
Do this reframing before writing the job statement, so the job-statement grammar operates on user-facing jobs.
avoid: Plan items describing how the system is built instead of what it does for the user.
Keeping implementation-flavored source text as a plan item instead of reframing it to a user-facing job or routing it to tests or architecture decision records.
core.why: The plan decomposes what the system does (user-facing jobs), not how it is built; implementation decisions belong reframed to the job they serve or in tests or architecture decision records.
evidence: Each plan item reads as a user-facing job the system performs (domain capability), not as how the system is built.
Every implementation-flavored source item is traceable either to a reframed user-facing job or to a test or architecture decision record it was routed to.
verification: Scope: plan artifacts (the profile's plan-artifact kinds) during planning/decomposition. The check does not cover authoring a test or architecture decision record that records a technology choice routed there from planning, nor coding work that implements an already-decomposed plan.

Whether a plan item states a user-facing job (domain capability: a user-facing job the system performs) and whether a source item is an implementation decision (technology choice) is judged semantically (LLM-judged); the realization carries the canonical example.

values: plan item not stated as a user-facing job the system performs

fires: A planner decomposes any feature request or source material into plan items.
A source or draft plan item reads like an implementation decision (a technology choice).
A draft plan item describes an internal mechanism, component or objective rather than a job the user gets done, even if it is not a technology choice.
doesNotFire: Authoring an architecture decision record or test that records a technology choice routed there from planning.
Coding work that implements an already-decomposed plan.

neutralityNotes: The convention is a planning-methodology rule and is almost entirely stack-neutral; nothing names a stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, suffix or path. Residual points: (1) 'test' and 'architecture decision record (ADR)' are kept as stack-neutral methodology vocabulary — the core needs no profile key for them because the obligation constrains plan content, not where routed artifacts live, and no ADR key exists in the closed vocabulary; (2) the canonical 'use redis for caching' example is retained only in the realization, which serves as the worked reference example; (3) 'the job grammar' was generalized to 'the job-statement grammar' because the enabling edge to the sibling rule is a realization graph fact; (4) 'acceptance' is treated as neutral ATDD vocabulary, while 'product capability'/'DESIRED OUTCOME' are stack-local plan-artifact names supplied by roles.plan_artifact.kinds or kept as realization task terms.
